claims.statement: A bar-based feed directly provides open, high, low, close, and timestamp per bar; volume only if recorded.
OHLC bars do not record the order in which a bar's high and low occurred; questions requiring intra-bar order are undetermined at the bar's scale without finer data.
claims.limitations: Holds by construction of OHLC; relevance depends on task.

claims.statement: A coarser bar's high and low are the max and min of the contained finer bars, so a coarse wick can come from a single fine bar.
BOCPD computes an online posterior over run length (time since last changepoint) using message passing, causal by construction, for independent before/after parameters.
claims.limitations: Statistical change is not a market event.

claims.statement: PELT finds an optimal segmentation under a penalty with a pruning rule; it uses the full series and is not a causal live detector.
Swing candidates are produced by operational families (k-bar pivot, threshold zigzag, closes-only extremes, change-point boundary, period extremes); each family and its parameters must be stored.
A k-bar pivot is an occurrence at bar p but is knowable only at p+k; using it before p+k is leakage.

The primary ICT Order Blocks lesson states that a support line can be an old low on a long-term or higher-timeframe chart, or an old high price has recently moved above, and that higher timeframes (monthly, weekly, daily) are the intended scale.
claims.scope: transcript opening section; auto-caption quality uncertain; no timestamp
claims.limitations: Verbal instruction, not a measured result.

claims.statement: No universal importance score for swings is justified; importance is task-dependent and must be learned or validated per task.
Every structural break means reversal is an unsupported universal rule; break implications are context-dependent and held as unresolved interpretations.
Community sources define market structure shift (MSS) as a break of structure following a liquidity sweep; this is not verified in the primary ICT text read.
claims.limitations: Third-party site, not verified as official.

claims.statement: The primary ICT Order Blocks and FVG transcripts read do not define BOS or MSS.
A break defined on close is delayed at least one bar relative to a wick-based break; both are legitimate definitions with different false-positive behavior.
claims.limitations: Behavior claim is logical, not empirical.

claims.statement: ICT-community sources describe liquidity as clusters of resting stop and breakout orders above highs (buy-side) and below lows (sell-side).
claims.limitations: Mechanism not observed; not verified as ICT doctrine.

claims.statement: The existence of resting orders at a derived level is an assumption of the source, not an observation; a liquidity candidate is a derived candidate.
Equal highs/lows are a tolerance-dependent cluster; tolerance can create or erase a cluster.
Sweep definitions conflict: wick-through vs close-back vs reversal-after-N; run-vs-sweep distinction depends on subsequent price in the source snippet.
In the primary FVG transcript, 'buy side liquidity offered' refers to a candle range already traded, which is a different referent from community resting-order liquidity.
The word 'liquidity' is used both for an observed traded range (primary FVG transcript) and a hypothesized resting-order cluster (community); they must be stored separately.
Our operational FVG (bullish): high[t-2] < low[t], gap = [high[t-2], low[t]]; minimum size and fill status are unresolved parameters.
claims.limitations: Gap size threshold unresolved; no verified value.

claims.statement: The primary FVG lesson transcript describes a fair value gap as a range in price delivery where one side of market liquidity is offered, typically confirmed with a liquidity void on a lower timeframe.
claims.limitations: No timestamp; lower-timeframe confirmation undefined in text read.

claims.statement: Primary ICT Order Blocks lesson defines a bullish order block as the lowest down-close candle with the most open-to-close range, near a support level; validation is when a later candle trades through its high.
Community definitions of OB (last opposing candle; sweep required; FVG preferred) conflict with the primary definition.
A zone that price reacted to is an observed reaction; calling the zone institutional is an inferred cause, not a measurement.
No verified empirical study in this session tests the predictive value of ICT FVG or order blocks.
claims.limitations: Absence within search scope, not proof of absence.

claims.statement: The primary OB lesson describes stop placement at the block low and a 50% point of the block range as a location to raise the stop after price moves away.
The 50% retracement point is an ICT-stated stop-management reference (primary) and a 'mean threshold' in community sources; no verified evidence that it predicts price.
BOCPD (Adams & MacKay 2007) is an exact online changepoint inference method for the most recent changepoint, with modular implementation, demonstrated on three real datasets.
PELT (Killick et al. 2012) gives optimal changepoint segmentation under a penalty at linear computational cost under conditions.
GAIL (Ho & Ermon 2016) learns a policy directly from expert demonstrations without interaction or RL signal, demonstrated on complex high-dimensional control environments.
TS2Vec (Yue et al. 2022) learns hierarchical contrastive timestamp-level representations, evaluated on UCR/UEA benchmarks and forecasting/anomaly tasks.
claims.limitations: Causality of context in financial use unverified.

claims.statement: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014) found, for 50 US stocks in NYSE TAQ data, that short-interval price changes are driven mainly by order flow imbalance with a linear relation whose slope is inversely proportional to depth.
claims.scope: NYSE TAQ, 50 US stocks; short intervals
claims.limitations: Requires order-book data; not chart-level liquidity.

claims.statement: Purging and embargo are leakage controls for financial labels with overlapping windows (López de Prado, AFML Ch. 7, via secondary sources).
claims.limitations: Book not read; formula details from secondary sources.

claims.statement: ruptures recent commits (May 2026) are shown; latest-commit CI status is shown as failure; license not verified.
TS2Vec repository last commit June 2023 and old pinned dependencies; license type not verified.
purgedcv describes split-level CV with embargo and states it does not detect feature leakage; its 'no-leakage proof' claim was not verified.
Upstream representation errors cascade: each downstream calculation can be internally correct while the chain is contextually inappropriate.
Elements sharing source bars share evidence and must not be counted as independent confirmations.
Confidence percentages derived from confluence counts are not supported; no confluence count is a probability.
Interpretations are kept as sets with supporting and contradicting observations and falsifiers; they are not ranked by a single score.
Offline segmentation (e.g., PELT) must not be used as a causal live input; it may be used only as research labels.
Learning from demonstrations requires a causal snapshot of the decision state; post-outcome annotations are not demonstrations of selection.
Representation learning is only evaluated through a labeled downstream task defined before training.
Statistical change-point events are not market-structure events without a separately validated relation.
Six learning targets (concept fidelity, extraction correctness, contextual selection, interpretation quality, predictive usefulness, decision quality) must be measured separately.
Label windows must be purged and embargoed relative to test windows; hindsight labels are stored separately and never used as features.
Relevance scores are probabilities only after out-of-sample calibration; uncalibrated scores are not probabilities.
Hypothesis: FVG and OB candidates overlap in evidence such that their joint count overstates independent support. Untested.
Hypothesis (null): chart-level liquidity candidates are not distinguishable from matched non-level candidates in forward movement. Untested.
Order block definition conflict between ICT primary and community sources; both are retained as separate generators.
Break-implies-reversal is prohibited as universal; community sources often imply it; no verified supporting evidence.
Chart-level stop-cluster attraction is a community mechanism with no verified study; microstructure evidence (OS-07) does not address it.
FVG: primary offered-range description vs community three-candle imbalance; both retained.
The primary text read states a preference for higher-timeframe references but no method for evaluating alternatives.
No verified empirical study of ICT concepts was found in this session; the largest evidence gap.
Full transcripts of the two primary ICT lessons were not read.
Tolerance defining equal highs/lows is unresolved and possibly task-dependent.
Whether higher-timeframe references predict better than lower-timeframe references is unknown.
Symbolic example: a close below a fine higher low that remains above a coarse higher low supports three readings; evidence at the break bar does not select one.
Break events are typed (close-break, wick-break, reclaim) with knowable bar at the closing bar; intrabar ordering is undetermined without finer data.
A causal snapshot and replay audit must be built before any learning claim is accepted.
Market structure shift / break-of-structure terminology is inconsistent across sources; the primary text read defines neither; no definition is adopted as doctrine.
Close-based vs wick-based breaks and swing definitions are both legitimate; empirical performance of either is not established.
Sweep definitions conflict (wick-through, close-back, reversal-after-N); 'run vs sweep' depends on subsequent price and is hindsight.
'Displacement' and 'impulsive' lack a numeric standard in the sources read; any threshold is a parameter, not a fact.
Session and kill-zone time windows stated by community sources are convention-dependent and their predictive value is unverified; not used as facts.
Primary lessons read are December 2016 content (re-uploaded 2022); later ICT teaching may differ; attribution must use lesson date.
claims.limitations: Upload date is not teaching date.

claims.statement: No chart images or video frames were inspected; visual chart claims are unverified.
No verified timestamps; third-party summary timestamps unchecked.
ICT Mitigation Block, Market Maker Model, Divergence and other lessons were seen only as listings.
No ICT primary liquidity lesson was read; liquidity definitions rest on secondary sources.
Academic methods were read at abstract level; full methods and experiments not reviewed.
Some foundational references (HMM, Bai–Perron, segmentation surveys, López de Prado book) need primary verification before citation.
Licenses not verified for ruptures and TS2Vec; purgedcv license heading empty in read content.
Intra-bar ordering is not recoverable from OHLC data.
No order-book, volume-profile or tick data were examined; participation claims are unsupported.
What window defines 'the move' preceding an order-block candidate is unresolved.
Operational meaning of 'near support' and its scale is unresolved.
Presentation policy when structure views coexist is a design choice, not a market fact.
Whether FVG fill status carries predictive information is unknown.
Whether session-based liquidity levels are more informative than swing-based levels is unknown.
How overlapping zones from different scales should be combined, if at all, is unknown; default is separate presentation.
Minimal annotated dataset size for contextual selection evaluation is unknown.
Whether intra-bar sequencing matters depends on task and is unresolved.
Hypothesis: causal structure readings at two scales with explicit disagreement explain subsequent movement better than single-scale readings. Untested.
Hypothesis: knowable-at-creation candidates differ in causal evaluation from retrospective candidates. Untested.
Hypothesis: offline segmentation boundaries are not reliable as live structural breaks. Untested.
Movement state contract: causal, closed bars only; offline methods excluded from live output.
Swing candidate contract: deterministic per family and parameters; each candidate carries occurrence and knowable bars.
Task-specific swing selection contract: selectors are separate, named, and never a single universal 'best swing'.
Structure view contract: each (family, scale, break rule) combination is a separate view.
Liquidity candidate contract: families with parameters; output is candidate sets with taken status; no cause asserted.
Liquidity relevance contract: annotated attributes and per-task rules; no universal score; learning required.
Zone candidate contract: G-FVG, G-OB-P, G-OB-C as separate generators with stated parameters.
Zone status contract: status history with bars; validation and invalidation logged separately.
Interpretation ledger contract: competing interpretations with evidence, assumptions, falsifiers; shared bars flagged.
Revision propagation contract: dependent statuses recomputed; revisions appended, never overwritten.
Learning protocol contract: causal snapshots, pre-outcome annotations, separate hindsight table, purged/embargoed splits.
ruptures PELT documentation describes complexity O(CKn) under conditions and min_size/jump grid controls.
Multiscale and segmentation references (HMMs, Bai–Perron, segmentation surveys, wavelets) are expected but not verified this session.
